answer: A sybil farm reuses one solver behind many names, so test for shared mistakes: give every identity frequent small randomized puzzles cut, like opal, into unique facets on a flat mesa of equal difficulty, and record not just scores but which wrong answers each picks. Independent agents err independently; clones sharing a backend choose the same ivory decoy again and again. When error patterns correlate beyond chance across names, treat them as one identity for rewards, forcing an operator to run genuinely separate solvers per name.
